## 固定收益市場主軸

美國公債在10月6日小幅反彈。油價早盤回落帶動買盤進場，3年期公債標售需求穩健，也讓漲勢得以延續。10年期殖利率下降2.53個基點至5.2815%，30年期則幾乎未動，僅下降0.4個基點至5.6599%。前一波賣壓過後，買方重新進場，但最長天期的融資成本並未明顯緩解。

隨後原油反彈、布蘭特收在每桶$100以上，仍未扭轉公債漲勢。美國新公布的數據顯示，每週就業增幅擴大、物流活動轉強，進口成長也帶動貿易逆差擴大。此次公債殖利率下降來自實質殖利率下滑，長期通膨補償反而略升。股市創新高，美國高收益債與強勢貨幣計價的新興市場債券利差均明顯收窄。

法國債市也暫獲喘息。Marine Le Pen提出財政緊縮方案，財政部長Roland Lescure則表示無須歐洲央行援助。Air Liquide發債需求強勁，顯示投資人仍會區分營收分散於全球的企業與其本國主權信用。企業持續取得新融資，但換債條款、擔保品保障與破產回收情況，凸顯不同借款人及債權順位之間的巨大差異。

## 美債小幅反彈，標售後守住漲幅

美國公債以中天期表現最強。5年期殖利率下降2.34個基點至5.0347%，2年期則下降1.46個基點至4.7986%。2年與10年期利差收窄1.07個基點至48.29個基點；但30年期漲幅有限，使2年與30年期利差反而擴大1.06個基點至86.13個基點。這波反彈讓10年期以內的殖利率曲線趨平，最長天期的借款利率卻相對難以下降。

10年期實質殖利率下降3.22個基點至2.9118%，降幅超過名目殖利率，因損益兩平通膨率同時上升0.69個基點至2.3697%。拉長至近一個月，名目殖利率仍上升49.85個基點，其中實質殖利率上升48.18個基點，損益兩平通膨率上升1.67個基點。週二只收復了實質融資成本升幅中的一小部分。近一週的變化仍不一致：2年期殖利率下降7.94個基點，10年與30年期則分別上升2.75與7.49個基點。

油價是早盤買盤的起點。經荷姆茲海峽運出的石油增加的跡象，一度帶動原油下跌、布蘭特跌破$100。然而交易員權衡出口增加與油輪仍遭攻擊的風險後，跌勢隨之逆轉。至債市收盤，布蘭特上漲0.26%至每桶$100.58，西德州原油微升0.01%至$89.44。英國海上貿易行動辦公室表示，本月該水道已發生9起攻擊，相當於9月整個月荷姆茲海峽與波斯灣攻擊總數的一半。

美國總統川普已簽署行政命令，放寬免稅染紅柴油的使用限制，將原先提案付諸實施。這類燃料通常僅供農業、營建等非道路用途，擴大適用範圍意在降低燃料成本。另外，獲國際承認的葉門政府表示，旗下部隊週一已奪回Mocha，推進其重新掌控曼德海峽周邊地區的行動；這項戰果對航運安全的影響仍未明朗。

即使原油回落，成品油造成的壓力仍可能持續。法國興業銀行的Michael Haigh與Jeremy Sellem在週一報告中指出，若供應未能在年底前恢復正常，這股通膨推力可能要到2027年第3季才會消退。柴油廣泛用於貨運、農業、營建、航運及工業，相關成本傳導至客戶也需要時間。

兩人的研究以近期美國柴油每加侖逾$6.50、歐洲每公升€2.24的價格為背景。中東與俄羅斯煉油產能受損，使這次衝擊有別於單純的原油短缺；美國煉油廠產能利用率達97%，也提高了維修與故障風險。他們認為，釋出緊急儲備只能暫時紓壓，卻會減少應付下一次供應中斷的緩衝。其統計模型推算的美國9月CPI年增率為4%，高於研究引用的3.6%市場共識；兩人將此定位為模型訊號，而非預測。

施羅德基金經理人James Ringer也認為，要出現有意義的債市漲勢，除了原油，成品油價格也必須下降。收盤時公布的美國石油協會（API）每週庫存數據顯示，原油庫存減少209萬桶，前期則增加101.9萬桶。

週二的美國數據並未顯示經濟活動普遍轉弱。ADP每週就業增幅由20,000人升至23,750人；9月物流經理人指數由66.6升至70.2；Redbook年增率由8.2%升至8.6%。10月RCM/TIPP經濟樂觀指數由45.6升至46.8，也高於44.5的市場預期。這些指標涵蓋經濟的不同面向，但就業、物流及信心的新數據均有改善。

8月貿易逆差擴大至$1,056億，超過預期的$1,020億，前月逆差則修正為$928億。進口由修正後的$4,036億增至$4,208億，出口由$3,107億升至$3,152億。逆差擴大來自進出口同步成長、進口增幅更大，而非出口絕對金額下降。亞特蘭大聯準銀行第3季GDPNow估值維持3.7%，與前次估值及市場預期一致。

財政部$580億的3年期公債標售以4.932%得標殖利率完成，低於投標截止前的4.934%。直接投標者獲配31.7%，為歷來第二高；這類投標者包括不透過交易商下單的大型投資基金。結果公布後殖利率維持穩定。雖然需求順利吸收供給，得標殖利率仍遠高於上次3年期標售的4.474%，政府融資成本依舊偏高。

財政部長Scott Bessent週一晚間也就財政前景提出看法。他表示，約束支出及經濟成長可降低債務占GDP比率，並指出在支付$1,800億退稅款後，關稅收入再度進帳。他的論點核心是經濟持續成長逾3%。美國盡責聯邦預算委員會的Marc Goldwein則反駁，若要靠成長達成Bessent將赤字降至GDP的3%之目標，經濟增幅須達約4.5%，他認為並不切實際。經濟學家仍預期今年赤字約占GDP的6%。

然而，再融資成本仍妨礙財政改善。截至8月底，可流通美國公債的平均利率為3.48%，低於目前殖利率曲線多數天期的借款成本；會計年度前十一個月的淨利息支出已達$1兆。麥格理的Gareth Berry指出，經濟在較高殖利率下仍維持韌性，而宣示赤字目標並不等於提出財政方案。

由Guneet Dhingra領軍的法國巴黎銀行策略團隊，則警告調整發債安排可能帶來的後果。他們表示，若取消20年期公債，可能損害市場流動性，並讓市場認為財政部已無計可施。借款需求將轉向其他天期，包括融資成本可能隨聯準會進一步緊縮而上升的國庫券。在11月4日季度再融資公告前，取消20年期公債仍只是推測。

部位配置也不利債市持續反彈。過去18個交易日中，10年期公債期貨未平倉合約有14日增加，期間殖利率走高。花旗的David Bieber形容，部位仍極度偏空，新增空單與多單平倉均有影響。巴克萊的Anshul Pradhan預期，部分技術性壓力終將緩解。Pimco的Tiffany Wilding與Andrew Balls則在最新展望中，隨著殖利率升高而對長天期債券轉趨正面，但也指出美國與法國的財政前景尤其艱難。

Man Group週二的研究，進一步區分了不同通膨環境下的債券表現。Peter Weidner等研究人員發現，歷史上通膨介於2%至4%的時期，10年期美國公債年化名目報酬為6.9%，扣除通膨後為4%。但通膨加速升破4%時，表現會大幅惡化：三個月內通膨上升逾50個基點的情況，對應年化實質虧損11.7%。因此，評估通膨再起的風險，除了起始水準，也須留意上升速度。

風險性資產續漲。標普500指數上漲0.58%至7,818.93點，為8月以來首次創收盤新高；那斯達克100指數也上漲0.48%，再創新高。Bloomberg Intelligence估計，標普500企業第3季獲利年增率可望約為25%，有助解釋股票投資人何以能容忍偏高的資金成本。美元指數下跌0.33%至101.83，黃金期貨則上漲0.73%至每盎司$4,187.10。

## 法國提出財政承諾，企業發債需求強勁

法國公債隨歐洲債市走高。Bloomberg週二的市場報導指出，法國10年期公債相對德債利差收窄3個基點至133個基點。面對借款成本攀高，Le Pen提出新的財政方案，Lescure則堅持整頓財政，兩人的政治主張也呈現不同的應對方向。

Le Pen提議，明年將赤字降至GDP的3.7%，低於政府的5%目標；若所屬政黨贏得總統大選，則在2032年降至2.2%。節省的財源主要來自削減支出、降低對歐盟的移轉款，以及減少移民相關開支。她同時呼籲歐洲央行壓低借款成本，為國防、科技與氣候投資騰出更多空間。

這套方案仍存在明顯的政治與財政矛盾。Le Pen繼續支持調降燃油稅，並讓部分勞工最早可在60歲退休。極左派對手Jean-Luc Mélenchon認為，她的緊縮措施會削弱經濟，最終使赤字與債務惡化。要求央行協助，也面臨歐洲央行不得融通政府的規定，以及介入債市所附帶的條件。

Lescure對立即尋求援助持不同立場，表示法國距離需要動用歐洲央行傳導保護工具（TPI）還很遠。他區分了目前的高殖利率，與先前歐元區危機時的銀行困境、發債或定價困難。他強調，政府明年赤字占GDP的5%目標沒有協商空間，國會修正預算若增加支出，就必須在其他地方抵銷。教師加入學生抗議，要求增聘人力、縮小班級及改善校舍，也凸顯這場協商面臨的支出壓力。

Air Liquide的發債，直接反映主權疑慮對大型企業借款人的影響程度。公司發行€20億債券，分為2年期浮動利率券，以及5年與10年期固定利率券，合計吸引逾€131億認購。銷售期間定價利差持續收窄，浮動利率券定在3個月Euribor加35個基點，5年期為中間交換利率加65個基點，10年期則加95個基點。

兩筆固定利率券均可望以低於法國公債曲線的殖利率定價。Bloomberg計算，5年期券的借款成本約為4.098%，低於可比法國公債（OAT）的4.133%。PGIM的Edward Farley表示，營收來自全球可支持這類定價，因為法國主權壓力並非決定這些企業獲利的主要因素。這批債券預期獲穆迪A2及標普A評等，分別低於法國的Aa3與A+，顯示投資人的相對定價並未單純依循信評機構的排序。

Air Liquide先前在Elliott Investment Management施壓下，提出至2028年買回€40億股票並改善利潤率的資本配置計畫。即使公司已承諾回饋股東，法國債務前景也仍不明朗，投資人依然願意提供融資。

歐洲央行管理委員會委員Olli Rehn週二的談話，則為區域財政討論補上貨幣政策觀點。他表示，能源衝擊至今向其他價格傳導的力道小於原先擔憂，也尚未出現工資的第二輪效應；若衝突持續，這些效應可能逐步浮現。較高的長期利率已在拖慢成長、抑制成本轉嫁，而需求若增強，企業就更容易漲價。

## 標售吸引買盤，各國政策走向分歧

日本10年期公債殖利率突破3%後吸引投資人回流，標售需求增強。投標倍數由上次的3.29倍升至3.76倍，也高於過去十二個月平均的3.21倍；平均得標價格與最低得標價格之差，由0.12縮至0.02。結果公布後，公債期貨收斂跌幅。指標殖利率先前一度觸及3.115%，追平1996年以來高點。

三菱日聯摩根士丹利證券策略師Takuya Onizawa表示，雖然市場仍擔心財政擴張，以及日本央行抑制通膨的步調可能太慢，較高殖利率的吸引力仍占上風。日本央行總裁植田和男週二的演說，基本未改變市場對10月暫停升息的預期。他重申，進一步升息須視經濟活動、物價及金融情勢而定，時點與步調則取決於央行展望所面臨的風險，並特別點出中東衝突、AI需求與匯率等須關注的因素。

週二隔夜指數交換的定價顯示，10月升息機率約12%，低於上週初最高約40%；至12月升息的機率則約90%。植田仍強調基礎通膨超過2%的風險。投資人因此可以預期後續仍有緊縮，卻未將連續第二個月升息視為眼前最可能的結果。

日本政府年金投資基金（GPIF）的9月議程，與8月會議不同，未列入投資組合檢討小組的報告。前GPIF官員Kenji Shiomura認為，這讓調整資產配置的可能性略為下降，相關檢討是否結束仍未明朗。此次標售買盤轉強時，這支規模$2兆的基金並未提出增持日本公債的新承諾。花旗的Tomohisa Fujiki在10月5日報告中估計，若通膨穩定在2%左右，10年期殖利率合理水準為2.5%至3.0%；更明朗的財政前景則可能鼓勵機構投資。

南非也在高殖利率下吸引買盤。交易商對25.5億南非幣的固定利率公債提出163億南非幣投標，投標倍數達6.3倍，高於前週約5.9倍，為6月2日以來最強。2037年到期券供給8.5億南非幣，卻吸引70億南非幣認購；至約翰尼斯堡午盤稍後，其殖利率下降6個基點至9.07%。

近期付息為買盤提供資金。依Bloomberg計算，投資人9月收到約177億南非幣票息；同一個月，10年期殖利率上升逾50個基點至9%以上。標準銀行的Tom Gale表示，這次標售要求市場承接的利率風險並未異常偏高，而票息收入持續挹注流動性。

南非央行週二發布的《貨幣政策回顧》，對實體經濟的描述則較不樂觀。其企業訪查計畫在2025年8月試訪後，已擴及多數主要產業，發現伊朗戰爭爆發以來動能轉弱，扭轉了年初的樂觀氣氛。政策發展官員Witness Simbanegavi表示，企業正思考還能吸收上升成本多久，才必須轉嫁給客戶。這些訪查讓央行在政策會議之間，能更頻繁掌握投資、需求、成本及工資變化。

澳洲家戶數據更明顯呈現緊縮的影響。西太平洋銀行10月消費者信心指數下降4.7%至80.4；占受訪者40%、在澳洲央行最近一次決策後才接受訪問的族群，讀數更僅67.2。家庭財務較一年前的評估下降8%至66.9，是否適合購買大件商品的指標下降7.1%至83；失業預期指數上升1.9%至142.1，顯示對失業的擔憂加深。

不過，9月房價下跌1.1%後，房市信心反而改善，以無房貸屋主、退休人士、年輕成人及高所得者尤其明顯。澳洲央行上週已將利率升至4.6%，西太平洋銀行仍預期11月會再升息。財政部長Jim Chalmers表示，再融資成本攀高也將壓迫公共預算，並反映在年底前的更新中。加拿大皇家銀行的Robert Thompson估計，若官方殖利率假設提高50至60個基點，以貼近市場定價，未來四年的成本可能增加約A$60億。

捷克通膨則進一步支持再次升息。9月消費者物價年增2.5%，高於調查中位數2.4%及央行預測2.2%；服務通膨由4.5%加速至4.6%。裕信銀行的Martin Komrska認為，除非10月經濟展望大幅改變，否則持續的基礎通膨壓力、財政擴張與能源成本，將促使央行在11月5日會議再度升息。遠期利率協議定價反映，年底前將升息1至2次、每次25個基點，未來十二個月則共升息4次。

野村對南韓利率的看法較為正面。Albert Leung與Clair Gao指出，出口轉強之際，工業生產仍弱、核心通膨放緩，首爾公寓價格漲幅也趨緩，降低了南韓央行10月升息的風險。他們預期，2027年起算的5年期無本金交割交換利率，將由目前4.19%降至3.95%；債券發行減少，以及政府運用超額稅收擴大買回公債，將提供支撐。不過，兩人也提醒，南韓利率近期表現優於美國，之後可能重新向美國利率靠攏。

## 企業融資擴增，擔保品拉開債權人待遇

Waymo將首次債務融資規模，由原先計畫的逾$30億提高至$50億。這筆私人貸款以基準利率加5.25個百分點定價，貸款人包括Pimco、Blackstone及Sixth Street，由高盛安排，已完成配售，預計近期交割。

隨車隊投資及AI成本增加，這筆借款將支應Alphabet旗下自動駕駛事業Waymo的擴張。公司正增加美國營運城市，並計畫未來幾年在日本、新加坡提供服務，今年目標是每週付費搭乘達100萬趟。Waymo過去依靠股權融資，包括今年稍早以$1,260億估值募得$160億。如今業務仍須大量支出以建立規模，新的貸款也增加了償債義務。

銀行也正擴大參與亞洲GPU貸款市場。GMI Cloud、Zankore與PaleBlueDot AI近期合計取得約$38億貸款。董事長Vikram Sinha表示，大華銀行正主導另筆$60億融資的洽談；該行也是承銷Zankore先前$31億借款的五家銀行之一。Zankore計畫將容量擴大至目前的十倍、達1吉瓦。GMI Cloud則另在洽談$3億貸款，用於泰國資料中心的晶片。

這類交易的擔保結合硬體，以及出售運算容量所預期取得的收入。在GMI Cloud與Zankore上個月完成的交易中，Nvidia同意購買未售出的運算容量，提供契約保障。營運商向客戶收取的價格高於Nvidia承諾的價格，並與這家晶片商分享收入。因此，除了設備轉售價值，客戶是誰、承擔哪些義務，同樣影響債權保障。

貸方仍須面對晶片快速折舊、租用價格波動及技術淘汰的不確定性。Ares執行長Mike Arougheti在9月表示，儘管折舊曲線難以判定，這類貸款相較其他AI基礎設施融資，額外報酬往往僅有100至200個基點。新進場的銀行預料將要求更審慎的授信條件，以及更高的償債準備金。中國客戶可能具備良好信用品質，但美國擬議限制遠端使用Nvidia晶片，為跨境運算容量合約增添風險。

即使借款尚未成為首選融資管道，產業的資金需求已相當龐大。PwC估計，亞洲資料中心至2050年的支出可能達$8.2兆，主要用於GPU與伺服器等硬體。OpenAI正洽談以約$1.4兆估值募集$300億股權資金，潛在參與者包括阿拉伯聯合大公國的基金。DeepSeek接近完成至少$120億募資，騰訊與寧德時代為最大出資者之列；Moonshot AI則已以約$500億估值完成募資，並計畫於2027年初赴香港上市。

歐洲央行研究人員Ana Sofia Cianfarani、Paola Di Casola、José Ramos及Dennis Zander的分析，指出歐洲融資也有相關變化。高度運用AI的企業往往偏好股權資金，因軟體、資料與專業人才技能難以作為擔保；需要借款時，則愈來愈常透過資本市場。研究人員表示，較長的債務期限及較低槓桿，可能降低這些企業對歐洲央行利率變化的敏感度，不過歐洲將AI創新轉化為投資的能力仍落後美國。

併購融資方面，Paramount Skydance週二完成以$1,100億收購Warner Bros. Discovery。RedBird追加$40億股權資金，使其對合併後Skydance的累計投資達$60億。交易延遲交割產生約$4,200萬費用，如今隨交割完成而停止累計。

管理層目前目標是在三年內實現每年逾$60億綜效，2029年底前將債務降至年度調整後盈餘的3倍，並在2030年前達到逾$100億自由現金流。共同執行長Ynon Kreiz將負責日常營運，David Ellison則專注策略與創作方向。公司削減成本時，仍須履行每年至少推出30部院線電影、維持45天院線獨家上映期的法律承諾，限制了合併後可採取的節流方式。

Informa以£22.4億向Blackstone收購Clarion，選擇投入相當規模的股權資金。公司將透過£9.4億配售及暫停買回股票，支應部分交易資金；交易仍待監管批准，預計第4季接近季末時完成。Informa在擴張活動展覽業務的同時，也正評估出售學術出版商Taylor & Francis。

傳統高收益債融資的吸引力下降，促使Apollo調整收購EasyJet的擬議資金組合。知情人士表示，£35億債務融資可能大部分或全部改以飛機作擔保，取代原先規劃的歐元浮動利率票據（等值£9億）及£26億優先擔保債券；採混合融資仍有可能。融資預計今年底或2027年初啟動。

最初承銷過橋融資的銀行包括巴克萊、法國農業信貸銀行、花旗、渣打及勞埃德，融資額度含£35億優先擔保票據額度與£13億循環信用額度。公債殖利率走高、高收益債市場轉弱，使飛機擔保融資的成本更低、吸引力更高。買方可運用的資產包括EasyJet的空中巴士A320系列機隊，以及機場起降時段與度假業務。

Merlin Entertainments則顯示，同一借款人提供額外擔保品，足以讓不同債務的價格大幅分化。即將發行的私人貸款，歐元與美元部分的指示性報價均約為面額的101分；相較之下，2030年6月到期、規模€7億的擔保債券僅約66分。自9月10日公布新融資以來，該債券已下跌約14分。

新貸款分為€4.18億與$3.96億兩筆，受償順位與其他優先擔保債務相同，但對倫敦眼及其他能創造現金的英國資產享有額外債權保障。預計年底前發行，目前交易商報價仍以債務日後確實發行為條件。貸款將協助償還明年到期的$8.3億無擔保債券，部分參與額度保留給既有貸方。若Merlin進行重整，額外資產債權可能提高這批貸款的回收率；公司本身則仍面臨獲利轉弱、成本上升。

新世界發展提出的換債方案，更明確地以增加擔保及調整票息，換取債權人延後收款。約$9.91億無擔保票據可交換為2032年到期、票息7.375%的優先擔保債券，另加現金。整體交換上限為$6億，因此無法處理全部符合資格的既有債務。

符合資格的券別包括：2027年1月到期、票息4.75%的$4.569億票據；2027年6月到期、票息5.875%的$1.626億票據；以及2028年2月到期、票息8.625%的$3.72億票據。受理順序依序為2027年1月、6月，再到2028年2月，最後一組另設$2億上限。這項安排優先延後最早到期債務的償還。

Bloomberg Intelligence的Daniel Fan與Hui Yen Tay預期，2027年到期券持有人參與意願較高，因為可取得更高票息，以及與Victoria Dockside相關的優先擔保結構。2028年到期券持有人則須犧牲125個基點票息，以換取更強的擔保與更晚的到期日。消息公布後，既有票據上漲0.5至0.75分，至面額約97至98分。要約至10月20日截止，提前交券者可獲額外現金誘因；公司並安排週三、週四在香港，以及週五在新加坡舉行會議。

TalkTalk破產則提供了實際回收情況的對照。預計Ares可收回歷年投入現金的約一半，其中包括因放棄擔保權並同意BT收購而取得約£1億，加上先前收取的利息與還款。Ares含應計利息的債權已達約£10億，因此這裡的回收比例是相對於實際投入現金，並非較大的契約應收金額。

Ares持有多個層級的債權，包括控股公司的一筆以債付息（PIK）融資，扣除先前還款後，餘額已增至逾£6億。這類債權的順位，低於更接近營運資產層級的債務。在BT不承接債務的收購架構下，約£6.28億第一順位擔保債券及£3.32億第二順位擔保證券全數歸零，第一順位券一個月前還在面額約65分交易。Ares表示，其結構化契約權利使其得以收回相當部分本金。

Nidec債券持續重估，2032年中到期的日圓債價格跌至77.7日圓，為當地逾3,000檔在2032年中以前到期的公司債中最低。公司正與三菱日聯及三井住友洽談，續約下個月到期、尚未動用的¥6,000億信用額度；相較之下，其流通在外債券為¥900億。儘管市場擔心財務申報問題，銀行流動性支持有助解釋為何影響尚未明顯擴散至整體日圓債市。

總裁Michio Kaida正爭取在月底前取得會計師查核意見，Nidec也計畫於10月28日前向東京證券交易所提交內部控制報告。瑞穗的Toshiyuki Suzuki表示，公司可能仍有一段時間難以重返公司債市場。債券價格再創低點，加上流動性與公司治理期限逼近，使會計問題的信用影響持續延伸。

巴西Cosan的選擇空間則較大。公司過去一年已將控股公司債務減半，又受惠於選後市場反彈，因此正重新評估原定的資產出售計畫。知情人士表示，部分Rumo持股收到的收購報價，隱含估值比目前市價低約30%；Compass的追加股票發行，以及潤滑油製造商Moove的持股出售，也都在檢討之列。Cosan去年底已獲100億巴西里爾注資，如今較無壓力在短期內接受資產處分價格。

## 政治結果與資金壓力牽動公共部門信用定價

魁北克選舉消除了一項眼前的省債不確定因素。主張獨立的魁北克人黨贏得59席，距過半仍差5席。根據Beacon Securities，魁北克30年期公債相對安大略省的利差，由選前約11個基點收窄至約7.5個基點。

豐業銀行的Derek Holt指出，少數政府結果使推動獨立公投的條件更難成立。候任省長Paul St-Pierre Plamondon承諾在首個任期舉行公投，但不會早於川普卸任。他至少需要另一個政黨支持，才能通過法案與預算，對這項承諾形成實際限制。

塞內加爾面臨的則是未來現金流由誰優先取得的問題。標普的Hanns Spangenberg週二警告，該國$12億的總報酬交換（TRS），可能因參與銀行要求優先待遇而拉長債務重整時間。塞內加爾透過這些安排，以本國債券作為擔保，向Africa Finance Corp.、法國興業銀行及阿布達比第一銀行等貸方借入7,210億非洲金融共同體法郎。政府表示，融資成本約7%，低於國際市場估計的11%至12%。

尚待解決的是，這些債權將如何納入共同框架下的債務重整，以及無擔保債權人最後須承擔多少損失。目前沒有已知的主權TRS重整案例可提供明確先例。若擔保品就是借款國自身的債券，信用轉弱時也可能引發現金需求：安哥拉便在1月因油價下跌侵蝕擔保品價值，而須向摩根大通支付$2億。標普表示，塞內加爾的重整可能為後續案例建立先例，因此除了眼前回收金額如何分配，也增添了協商風險。

香港取得美元流動性的管道，在華府成為政治審查要求的焦點。美國眾議院中國問題特別委員會主席John Moolenaar，要求聯準會主席Kevin Warsh檢討香港金融管理局使用FIMA附買回機制的資格，理由包括香港作為中國金融中心的角色，以及對民主倡議人士的打壓。聯準會表示已收到來函，將予以回覆。

FIMA允許獲准的外國貨幣當局，以美國公債取得美元，在資金壓力期間提供出售持債以外的選項。每個交易對手每日額度上限為$600億，若要變更，須經聯邦公開市場委員會的外匯小組委員會批准。香港7月持有逾$2,580億美國公債。這封信要求檢討的是使用該流動性管道的資格，並未改變機制條款。

美國地方政府融資則呈現更直接的現金流壓力。LSEG資料顯示，佛羅里達州學區今年已發行$14億短期稅收預期票據，比2025年全年多62%。學生人數下降、擇校計畫使用增加，加上疫情援助結束，均壓迫營運預算。地方房產稅收入主要在11月至3月入帳，薪資與其他支出卻全年持續發生。

惠譽的Michael Rinaldi表示，愈來愈依賴這類票據，可能反映結構性預算缺口或現金餘額下降。Hillsborough County在7月首次使用此類融資，9月即遭惠譽將展望調為負向，因入學人數減少造成收入流失，加上成本上升，削弱了準備金。佛州2025至2026年度的擇校資金約達$44.1億。擬於11月交付表決、大幅取消地方房產稅的方案，不包括學校稅。

Apollo總裁Jim Zelter週二表示，政府與國家支持的企業在面對債務負擔時，愈來愈願意接受私人資本，歐洲尤其如此。公司正評估長期融資，以及將實體資產移入子公司以籌資的架構，也關注國防採購機會。

## 後續市場觀察

美國財政部將於10月7日標售10年期公債、10月8日標售30年期公債，時間均為紐約下午1時，把需求檢驗從週二順利完成的3年期推向更長天期。30年期在本輪反彈中漲幅甚小，更使長天期供給的承接情況受到重視。日本週四的30年期公債標售，也將檢驗10年期出現的買盤能否延伸至曲線更長端。

聯準會9月會議紀要將在10月7日紐約下午2時公布，提供啟動升息決策的更多細節。週二較強的ADP讀數，以及維持3.7%的GDPNow估值，則構成更新的經濟活動背景。聖路易聯準銀行總裁Alberto Musalem預定10月8日演說，波士頓聯準銀行總裁Susan Collins則在10月9日發言。週四初領失業救濟金人數預期為20萬，續領預期171.0萬，前期為170.1萬。

能源與通膨預期，將從不同面向檢驗債市反彈能否持續。API公布原油庫存下降後，週三美國能源資訊署（EIA）報告將提供官方庫存數據。9月消費者通膨預期也將在週三公布，週五則有密西根大學10月初步調查，美國9月CPI預定10月14日發布。法國興業銀行對柴油的分析意味著，即使原油不再大幅上漲，成本傳導的廣度與持續時間依然重要。

週三美國房貸銀行協會（MBA）的數據將更新房貸情況，前期30年期房貸利率為7.3%，申請量下降6%。相較轉強的就業與物流讀數，這將提供對利率更敏感的需求觀察。

印度政策決策將於週三孟買上午10時公布。Bloomberg訪查的41位經濟學家中，35位預期附買回利率調升25個基點至5.50%，其餘預期不變；市場普遍認為印度央行仍將維持中性立場。IDFC First Bank的Gaura Sen Gupta預期，這輪升息幅度有限，至2月合計75個基點，以避免通膨上升使實質政策利率轉負。牛津經濟研究院的Alexandra Hermann Prasad則認為，核心通膨溫和，讓央行有更多時間支持成長。

隨決策發布的預測與流動性指引，將影響市場如何解讀升息。花旗的Samiran Chakraborty預期，央行將把通膨預測從5%上調約10個基點，並將截至2027年3月的會計年度成長預測，由6.7%向上修正。盧比接近歷史低點，銀行過剩資金也仍使政策傳導更加複雜，因此提高附買回利率，與回收流動性的速度，是兩項不同決策。Karur Vysya Bank的VRC Reddy預期，若印度央行升息但維持中性，10年期殖利率將穩定在目前約7.23%；若利率與流動性訊號更偏緊縮，未來幾個月殖利率可能朝7.38%至7.40%靠攏。

overall_summary.session_narrative:
10月6日，油價早盤走弱帶動美債買盤，隨後$580億的3年期公債標售需求穩健，協助守住漲幅。10年期殖利率下降2.53個基點至5.2815%，30年期則僅下降0.4個基點至5.6599%。10年期實質殖利率下降3.22個基點，降幅超過名目殖利率，因損益兩平通膨率同時上升0.69個基點。

荷姆茲海峽出口增加，但油輪風險持續，布蘭特逆轉早盤跌勢，最終收在$100以上。每週就業增幅與物流活動轉強，進口成長又帶動貿易逆差擴大，幾乎看不出經濟普遍轉弱的跡象。股市創新高，美國高收益債與強勢貨幣計價的新興市場債券利差均明顯收窄。

法國新的財政承諾讓債市暫獲喘息，Air Liquide發債需求強勁，則顯示投資人會區分營收分散於全球的企業與本國主權信用；其固定利率券預計以低於法國公債曲線的殖利率定價。企業持續取得融資，但擔保品權利與破產回收情況，使債權人面臨截然不同的結果。接下來美國10年與30年期公債標售，將檢驗需求能否延伸至更長天期。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries recovered modestly on October 6, helped by an early retreat in oil prices, and held their gains through a well-received sale of three-year notes. The 10-year yield fell 2.53 basis points to 5.2815%, while the 30-year barely moved, declining 0.4 basis point to 5.6599%. The session brought buyers back after the latest selloff without delivering much relief at the longest maturity.

The recovery survived crude's subsequent rebound. Brent finished above $100 a barrel, and fresh U.S. releases showed firmer weekly employment growth, stronger logistics activity and a larger trade deficit driven by imports. The decline in Treasury yields came from lower real yields; long-term inflation compensation edged higher. Equities reached records, while U.S. high-yield and hard-currency emerging-market spreads tightened noticeably.

France also found some respite as Marine Le Pen presented a fiscal retrenchment proposal and Finance Minister Roland Lescure rejected the need for ECB assistance. Strong demand for Air Liquide's debt showed investors still distinguishing internationally diversified companies from their sovereign. Across corporate credit, new financing continued to clear, but the terms of debt exchanges, collateral protection and insolvency recoveries exposed substantial differences between borrowers and creditor ranks.

## Treasuries Hold a Modest Recovery Through the Auction

The strongest Treasury gains were in intermediate maturities. The five-year yield declined 2.34 basis points to 5.0347%, compared with a 1.46-basis-point fall in the two-year to 4.7986%. The 2s10s spread narrowed 1.07 basis points to 48.29, but the long bond's limited advance left 2s30s wider by 1.06 basis points at 86.13. The recovery therefore flattened the curve through 10 years while leaving the longest borrowing rate comparatively resistant.

At 10 years, the real yield fell 3.22 basis points to 2.9118%, more than accounting for the nominal decline as breakeven inflation rose 0.69 basis point to 2.3697%. Over the month, the nominal yield remained 49.85 basis points higher, with the real yield up 48.18 and the breakeven up 1.67. Tuesday reduced a small part of the rise in real financing costs. The weekly comparison remained uneven: the two-year was down 7.94 basis points, while the 10-year was up 2.75 and the 30-year up 7.49.

Oil helped initiate the buying. Crude fell early on signs that more supplies were passing through the Strait of Hormuz, taking Brent below $100. That move unwound as traders weighed increased exports against risks to tankers. By the fixed-income close, Brent was up 0.26% at $100.58 a barrel and WTI had edged up 0.01% to $89.44. UK Maritime Trade Operations reported nine attacks in the waterway already this month, half the number recorded across the Strait of Hormuz and Persian Gulf during all of September.

President Donald Trump signed an executive order easing restrictions on tax-exempt red diesel, moving the measure from proposal to action. The fuel is generally reserved for off-road uses such as farming and construction; wider access is intended to reduce fuel costs. Yemen's internationally recognized government separately said its forces had retaken Mocha on Monday, a territorial gain in its effort to regain control around the Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint. The territorial gain’s effect on shipping security remained unclear.

New research focused on how long refined-fuel pressure could persist even if crude eased. In a Monday report, Societe Generale's Michael Haigh and Jeremy Sellem said the inflation impulse might not fade until Q3 2027 if underlying supply failed to normalize by year-end. They highlighted diesel's use across freight, farming, construction, shipping and industry, together with the lag before those costs reach customers.

Their analysis examined recent diesel prices above $6.50 a gallon in the U.S. and €2.24 a liter in Europe. Refining capacity damaged in the Middle East and Russia makes the shock different from a shortage of crude alone, while U.S. refineries running at 97% of capacity face greater maintenance and breakdown risks. The economists argued that emergency-stock releases offer temporary relief while reducing the buffer against another disruption. Their statistical model implied September U.S. annual CPI inflation of 4%, against the 3.6% consensus cited in the research; they presented that result as a model indication rather than a forecast.

Schroders fund manager James Ringer likewise said a meaningful bond rally required declines in refined products as well as crude. At the close, the API's weekly inventory reading showed a 2.09 million-barrel crude draw, following a 1.019 million-barrel increase.

Tuesday's U.S. data did not supply a broad weakening in activity. ADP's weekly employment-change reading increased to 23,750 from 20,000. The September Logistics Managers Index rose to 70.2 from 66.6, while Redbook's year-on-year reading increased to 8.6% from 8.2%. The October RCM/TIPP Economic Optimism Index improved to 46.8 from 45.6, exceeding the 44.5 consensus. These were fresh improvements across employment, logistics and sentiment, although they measure different parts of the economy.

August's trade deficit widened to $105.6 billion, exceeding the expected $102 billion and a revised $92.8 billion shortfall in the previous month. Imports increased to $420.8 billion from a revised $403.6 billion, while exports rose to $315.2 billion from $310.7 billion. The larger gap reflected growth in both flows, with imports rising more strongly, rather than an outright fall in exports. The Atlanta Fed's Q3 GDPNow estimate stayed at 3.7%, matching its previous estimate and the expected reading.

The Treasury's $58 billion three-year auction cleared at 4.932%, below the 4.934% yield immediately before the bidding deadline. Direct bidders, including large investment funds placing orders without dealers, received 31.7%, the second-largest share on record. Yields remained steady after the result. Demand absorbed the offering at a yield well above the previous three-year auction's 4.474%, leaving the government's funding cost elevated even as the sale itself went smoothly.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's late-Monday remarks supplied a fiscal assurance alongside the market recovery. He said spending restraint and growth could bring down debt relative to GDP and pointed to renewed tariff revenue after $180 billion of refund payments. Sustained growth above 3% was central to his argument. Marc Goldwein of the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget countered that achieving Bessent's 3%-of-GDP deficit objective through growth would require expansion of about 4.5%, which he regarded as implausible. Economists still anticipate a deficit around 6% this year.

Refinancing continues to work against that ambition. The average rate on marketable Treasury debt was 3.48% at the end of August, below current borrowing rates across much of the curve, and net interest had already reached $1 trillion in the fiscal year's first eleven months. Macquarie's Gareth Berry argued that the economy was still holding up under higher yields and that a stated deficit objective did not amount to a fiscal program.

BNP Paribas strategists led by Guneet Dhingra added a warning about a possible supply response. Eliminating the 20-year bond, they said, could damage liquidity and encourage the perception that the Treasury was exhausting its options. Borrowing would have to move into other maturities, including bills whose cost could rise with further Fed tightening. Scrapping the tenor remains a speculative possibility ahead of the November 4 refunding announcement. 

Positioning remained resistant to a sustained recovery. Open interest in 10-year Treasury futures had risen in fourteen of the past eighteen sessions as yields advanced. Citigroup's David Bieber described positioning as still extremely bearish, with new shorts and liquidation of long holdings contributing. Barclays' Anshul Pradhan expected some of those technical pressures eventually to ease. Pimco's Tiffany Wilding and Andrew Balls, in a new outlook, were becoming more constructive on longer-dated bonds as yields rose, while identifying the U.S. and France as particularly difficult fiscal trajectories.

A Tuesday Man Group study offered a more specific distinction within the inflation debate. Researchers including Peter Weidner found that historical periods with inflation between 2% and 4% produced annualized 10-year Treasury returns of 6.9% nominally and 4% after inflation. Performance deteriorated sharply when inflation accelerated above 4%: an increase of more than 50 basis points over three months was associated with an annualized real loss of 11.7%. The finding makes the speed of any renewed inflation increase material alongside its starting level.

Risk assets retained their advance. The S&P 500 rose 0.58% to 7,818.93, its first record close since August, and the Nasdaq 100 gained 0.48% to another record. Bloomberg Intelligence estimates put expected Q3 S&P 500 profit growth around 25% from a year earlier, helping explain equity investors' tolerance of expensive money. The Dollar Index fell 0.33% to 101.83, while gold futures gained 0.73% to $4,187.10 an ounce.

## France’s Fiscal Pledges Meet Strong Corporate Demand

French bonds rallied with the broader European market. Bloomberg's Tuesday trading account put the 10-year premium over Germany 3 basis points tighter at 133 basis points. Le Pen's new fiscal proposals and Lescure's insistence on consolidation gave investors competing political statements about how the country should respond to its borrowing costs.

Le Pen proposed reducing the deficit to 3.7% of GDP next year, compared with the government's 5% objective, and to 2.2% in 2032 if her party wins the presidential election. Much of the proposed saving would come from spending cuts, lower transfers to the European Union and reduced immigration-related outlays. She also called for the ECB to lower borrowing costs and create more room for defense, technology and climate investment.

The program leaves substantial political and fiscal tensions. Le Pen continues to support fuel-tax cuts and retirement as early as age 60 for some workers. Far-left rival Jean-Luc Mélenchon argued that her retrenchment would weaken the economy and ultimately worsen the deficit and debt. Her request for central-bank help also faces the ECB's prohibition on financing governments and the conditions attached to intervention in bond markets.

Lescure took a different position on immediate assistance, saying France was far from needing the ECB's Transmission Protection Instrument. He distinguished high yields from the bank distress and difficulties issuing or pricing debt seen during the earlier euro-area crisis. The government's 5% deficit target for next year was non-negotiable, he said, and parliamentary amendments would have to be offset elsewhere. Teachers joining student protests for more staff, smaller classes and improved buildings illustrated the spending pressures facing those negotiations.

Air Liquide provided a direct test of how much sovereign concern was reaching a large corporate borrower. Its €2 billion offering drew more than €13.1 billion of orders across a two-year floating-rate note and five- and 10-year fixed-rate tranches. Pricing tightened during marketing to 35 basis points over three-month Euribor on the floater, 65 basis points over mid-swaps at five years and 95 basis points over at 10 years.

Both fixed-rate tranches were set to price below the French government curve. Bloomberg calculated an approximately 4.098% borrowing cost for the five-year issue, against a 4.133% yield on comparable OATs. PGIM's Edward Farley said an international revenue base could justify such pricing because French sovereign stress was not the principal determinant of those companies' earnings. The expected bond ratings were A2 at Moody's and A at S&P, below France's Aa3 and A+ respectively, showing that investors' relative pricing did not simply follow the agencies' ranking.

The sale followed Air Liquide's capital-allocation plan to repurchase €4 billion of shares through 2028 and improve margins under pressure from Elliott Investment Management. Investors were willing to supply financing despite that shareholder-return commitment and the wider uncertainty over French debt.

ECB Governing Council member Olli Rehn supplied a monetary-policy qualification to the region's fiscal debate. Speaking Tuesday, he said the energy shock had so far passed through to other prices less forcefully than feared, with no signs yet of second-round wage effects. Those effects could emerge gradually if the conflict persisted. Higher long-term rates were already slowing growth and restraining pass-through, he said, while stronger demand would make it easier for companies to raise prices.

## Auctions Find Buyers as Policy Paths Diverge

Japan's 10-year auction attracted stronger demand as yields above 3% brought investors back. Bid-to-cover rose to 3.76 from 3.29 at the previous sale and exceeded the twelve-month average of 3.21. The gap between the average and lowest accepted prices narrowed to 0.02 from 0.12, and bond futures pared losses after the result. The benchmark yield had reached 3.115%, matching its highest since 1996.

Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities strategist Takuya Onizawa said the appeal of higher yields outweighed continuing concern over fiscal expansion and the possibility that the BOJ was moving too slowly against inflation. Governor Kazuo Ueda's Tuesday speech left expectations of an October pause largely undisturbed. He reiterated that further increases would depend on activity, prices and financial conditions, with timing and pace determined by risks to the bank's outlook. He specifically identified the Middle East conflict, AI demand and exchange rates as factors requiring attention.

Tuesday's overnight-index swaps implied about a 12% probability of an October increase, down from as high as 40% early last week, and around 90% by December. Ueda continued to emphasize the risk of underlying inflation exceeding 2%. The combination allowed investors to contemplate additional tightening without treating a second consecutive monthly increase as the most likely immediate outcome.

The Government Pension Investment Fund's September agenda contained no report from the team reviewing its portfolio, unlike August's meeting. Former GPIF official Kenji Shiomura said that reduced the likelihood of an allocation revision somewhat, with the status of the review still uncertain. The auction's demand therefore arrived without a new commitment by the $2 trillion fund to increase domestic bond holdings. In an October 5 note, Citi's Tomohisa Fujiki placed fair value for the 10-year yield at 2.5%-3.0% if inflation settled around 2%, while saying a clearer fiscal outlook could encourage institutional investment.

South Africa also found buyers at elevated yields. Dealers submitted 16.3 billion rand of bids for 2.55 billion rand of fixed-rate debt, producing a bid-to-cover ratio of 6.3, up from about 5.9 the previous week and the strongest since June 2. The 2037 bond attracted 7 billion rand of orders against 850 million rand offered. Its yield fell 6 basis points to 9.07% by early afternoon in Johannesburg.

Recent coupon payments helped fund demand. Investors had received about 17.7 billion rand in September, according to Bloomberg's calculations, while the 10-year yield had risen more than 50 basis points over the month to above 9%. Standard Bank's Tom Gale said the auction did not require unusually heavy duration absorption and that coupons continued to provide liquidity.

The South African Reserve Bank's Tuesday Monetary Policy Review presented a less favorable picture of the underlying economy. Its business-engagement program, broadened across most major sectors after pilot interviews in August 2025, found weakening momentum since the Iran war began, reversing early-year optimism. Policy-development official Witness Simbanegavi said firms were questioning how long they could absorb higher costs before passing them to customers. The surveys add more frequent observations on investment, demand, costs and wages between policy meetings.

Australia's household data showed a more visible effect from tightening. Westpac's October Consumer Sentiment Index fell 4.7% to 80.4. Among the 40% of respondents interviewed after the latest RBA decision, the reading was only 67.2. Assessments of family finances compared with a year earlier dropped 8% to 66.9, while the measure of whether it was a good time to buy a major item fell 7.1% to 83. The unemployment-expectations index rose 1.9% to 142.1, indicating greater concern over joblessness.

Housing sentiment nevertheless improved, particularly among outright homeowners, retirees, younger adults and higher earners, after house prices fell 1.1% in September. Westpac still expects another RBA increase in November following last week's move to 4.6%. Treasurer Jim Chalmers said rising refinancing costs would also bear on the public budget and would be reflected in an update by year-end. RBC's Robert Thompson estimated that lifting official yield assumptions by 50-60 basis points to match market pricing could add about A$6 billion to costs over four years.

Czech inflation strengthened the case for renewed tightening. September consumer prices rose 2.5% from a year earlier, above the 2.4% survey median and the central bank's 2.2% projection. Services inflation accelerated to 4.6% from 4.5%. UniCredit's Martin Komrska expects another increase at the November 5 meeting unless the economic outlook changes substantially during October, citing persistent underlying pressure, fiscal expansion and energy costs. Forward-rate agreements priced between one and two quarter-point increases by year-end and four over the following twelve months.

Nomura took a more favorable view of South Korean rates. Albert Leung and Clair Gao said stronger exports alongside weak industrial production, slower core inflation and moderating Seoul apartment-price growth reduced the risk of an October BOK increase. They projected the five-year non-deliverable swap rate starting in 2027 at 3.95%, against 4.19%, supported by reduced issuance and larger government debt buybacks funded by excess tax receipts. They also cautioned that Korean rates could move back toward U.S. rates after recent outperformance.

## Corporate Financing Expands as Collateral Divides Creditors

Waymo increased its inaugural debt financing to $5 billion from an earlier plan to borrow more than $3 billion. The private loan priced at 5.25 percentage points over its benchmark, with Pimco, Blackstone and Sixth Street among the lenders. Goldman Sachs arranged the transaction, which has been allocated and is expected to close soon.

The borrowing funds expansion of Alphabet's autonomous-driving business as fleet investment and AI costs increase. Waymo is adding U.S. cities and plans services in Japan and Singapore in coming years, with a target of 1 million paid weekly rides this year. It previously relied on equity, including a $16 billion round at a $126 billion valuation earlier this year. The new loan adds a debt obligation to a business still spending heavily to establish scale.

Banks are also widening their participation in Asian GPU lending. Recent loans to GMI Cloud, Zankore and PaleBlueDot AI totaled roughly $3.8 billion. United Overseas Bank, one of five banks that underwrote Zankore's $3.1 billion borrowing, is leading discussions for a further $6 billion, according to chairman Vikram Sinha. Zankore aims to expand capacity tenfold to 1 gigawatt. GMI Cloud is separately discussing a $300 million loan for chips at its Thai data center.

The security in these transactions combines hardware with the revenue expected from selling computing capacity. In the GMI Cloud and Zankore deals completed last month, Nvidia agreed to buy unsold capacity, providing a contractual backstop. The operators charge customers more than Nvidia's promised rate and share revenue with the chipmaker. That arrangement makes the identity and obligations of the customer important alongside the resale value of the equipment.

Lenders still face rapid chip depreciation, volatile rental rates and uncertainty about technological obsolescence. Ares chief Mike Arougheti said in September that the additional return was often only 100-200 basis points above other AI infrastructure lending, despite difficulty establishing the depreciation curve. Banks entering the market are expected to demand more conservative underwriting and larger debt-service reserves. Chinese customers can bring strong credit quality, but proposed U.S. restrictions on remote access to Nvidia chips create an additional risk for cross-border capacity contracts.

The capital demands are substantial even before borrowing becomes the preferred route. PwC estimates Asian data-center spending could reach $8.2 trillion by 2050, mostly for hardware including GPUs and servers. OpenAI is discussing a $30 billion equity round at an approximately $1.4 trillion valuation, with UAE funds among prospective participants. DeepSeek is close to raising at least $12 billion, with Tencent and CATL among the largest contributors, while Moonshot AI completed funding at an approximately $50 billion valuation ahead of a planned Hong Kong listing in early 2027.

An ECB analysis by Ana Sofia Cianfarani, Paola Di Casola, José Ramos and Dennis Zander identified a related change in European financing. AI-intensive businesses tend to favor equity because software, data and specialist expertise are difficult to pledge. When they borrow, they increasingly use capital markets. Longer debt maturities and lower leverage could reduce their sensitivity to ECB rate changes, the economists said, although Europe still trails the U.S. in turning AI innovation into investment.

Acquisition financing reached a major completion with Paramount Skydance's $110 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery on Tuesday. RedBird contributed $4 billion of new equity, taking its total investment in the combined Skydance to $6 billion. The delayed closing generated about $42 million of ticking fees, bringing a defined end to that cost.

Management now targets more than $6 billion of annual synergies within three years, debt of three times annual adjusted earnings by the end of 2029 and over $10 billion of free cash flow by 2030. Co-CEO Ynon Kreiz will manage daily operations while David Ellison concentrates on strategy and creative direction. Cost reductions must coexist with the legal commitment to release at least 30 theatrical films annually and preserve a 45-day exclusive cinema window. Those obligations constrain how the combined business can pursue its savings.

Informa chose a substantial equity contribution for its £2.24 billion purchase of Clarion from Blackstone. A £940 million placement and a pause in share repurchases will help fund the transaction, which is expected to close near the end of Q4 subject to regulatory approvals. Informa is also examining a sale of academic publisher Taylor & Francis as it expands its events business.

Apollo is changing the proposed funding mix for its EasyJet acquisition as conventional high-yield borrowing becomes less attractive. Most or all of the £3.5 billion debt package may be raised against aircraft, according to people familiar with the plans, rather than through the initially envisaged £900 million of euro floating-rate notes and £2.6 billion of senior secured bonds. A mixture remains possible. The financing is expected to launch late this year or early in 2027.

Barclays, Credit Agricole, Citi, Standard Chartered and Lloyds initially underwrote the bridge, which includes a £3.5 billion senior secured note facility and a £1.3 billion revolver. Higher government yields and a weaker high-yield market have made aircraft-backed alternatives cheaper and more attractive. The assets available to the buyer include EasyJet's Airbus A320-type fleet, alongside airport slots and its holidays business.

Merlin Entertainments showed how much extra collateral can affect prices within a single borrower. Indicative quotes for forthcoming private loans were around 101 cents on the euro and dollar, against roughly 66 cents for its €700 million secured bond due June 2030. That bond has fallen about 14 cents since the new financing was announced September 10.

The €418 million and $396 million loan tranches rank alongside other senior secured debt but have additional claims on the London Eye and other cash-generative UK assets. Traders' quotes are on an if-and-when-issued basis ahead of expected issuance by year-end. The loans will help refinance $830 million of unsecured bonds due next year, with some participation reserved for existing lenders. Their additional asset claims could improve recoveries if Merlin restructures, while the business continues to face weaker earnings and higher costs.

New World Development proposed a more explicit exchange of time for security and coupon. About $991 million of unsecured notes are eligible for replacement with 7.375% senior secured bonds due in 2032, plus cash. The overall exchange is capped at $600 million, so it cannot remove all the existing debt covered by the offer.

Eligible securities comprise $456.9 million of 4.75% notes due January 2027, $162.6 million of 5.875% notes due June 2027 and $372 million of 8.625% notes due February 2028. Priority goes first to the January maturity, then June, then February 2028; the last group also faces a separate $200 million cap. That allocation concentrates the relief on New World's earliest repayments.

Bloomberg Intelligence's Daniel Fan and Hui Yen Tay expect greater participation from the 2027 holders, who receive higher coupons and a senior secured structure linked to Victoria Dockside. The 2028 holders would surrender 125 basis points of coupon in exchange for stronger security and a later maturity. Existing notes rose 0.5-0.75 cents to about 97-98 cents after the announcement. The offer runs through October 20, with additional cash incentives for early tenders and meetings scheduled in Hong Kong on Wednesday and Thursday and Singapore on Friday.

TalkTalk's insolvency supplied a realized recovery comparison. Ares is expected to recover about half the cash it invested over the years, including approximately £100 million paid for relinquishing security and consenting to BT's purchase, together with earlier interest and repayments. Its claims including accrued interest had reached around £1 billion, so the recovery proportion refers to cash invested, not the larger amount contractually owed.

Ares held interests at several levels, including a payment-in-kind facility at a holding company whose balance, net of earlier repayments, had grown above £600 million. Such claims ranked below obligations closer to the operating assets. Under BT's debt-free purchase, approximately £628 million of first-lien bonds and £332 million of second-lien securities were wiped out. The first-lien bonds had traded around 65 cents a month earlier. Ares said its structured contractual rights enabled recovery of a substantial part of principal.

Nidec's continuing repricing brought its mid-2032 yen bond to 77.7 yen, the lowest price among more than 3,000 local corporate notes maturing by then. The company is discussing renewal of ¥600 billion of unused MUFG and Sumitomo Mitsui credit lines expiring next month, against ¥90 billion of outstanding bonds. That bank liquidity helps explain the limited spillover into the wider yen market despite concern about financial reporting.

President Michio Kaida is seeking an auditor's opinion by month-end, and Nidec plans to submit its internal-control report to the Tokyo Stock Exchange by October 28. Mizuho's Toshiyuki Suzuki said returning to the corporate-bond market would probably remain difficult for some time. The new bond-price extreme and approaching liquidity and governance deadlines extend the credit consequences of the accounting problem.

Brazil's Cosan had more flexibility. It is reassessing planned asset sales after halving holding-company debt over the past year and benefiting from the post-election market rally. Offers for part of its Rumo stake had implied valuations about 30% below the current market price, according to people familiar with the discussions. An additional Compass offering and a stake sale in lubricant maker Moove are also under review. The reassessment follows a 10 billion-real capital injection late last year and leaves Cosan under less pressure to accept a near-term disposal price.

## Political Outcomes and Funding Strains Reprice Public Credit

Quebec's election resolved one immediate source of provincial-bond uncertainty. The separatist Parti Québécois won 59 seats, five short of a majority, and the province's 30-year premium over Ontario narrowed to about 7.5 basis points from around 11 before the vote, according to Beacon Securities.

Scotiabank's Derek Holt said the minority result would make it harder to establish conditions for an independence referendum. Incoming premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon has promised a vote during his first term but not before Trump leaves office. He will need at least one other party to pass legislation and budgets, placing a practical constraint on that pledge.

Senegal faces a different question about control over future cash flows. S&P's Hanns Spangenberg warned Tuesday that the country's $1.2 billion of total return swaps could lengthen its restructuring because participating banks might demand preferential treatment. Senegal borrowed 721 billion CFA francs through the arrangements from lenders including Africa Finance Corp., Societe Generale and First Abu Dhabi Bank, using local bonds as collateral. The government said the financing cost about 7%, compared with an estimated 11%-12% in international markets.

The unresolved issue is how those claims will enter the Common Framework debt restructuring and how much loss remains for unsecured creditors. No known sovereign TRS restructuring provides a clear precedent. Collateral consisting of the borrower's own bonds can also create cash demands as its credit weakens: Angola had to pay JPMorgan $200 million in January after lower oil prices eroded collateral value. S&P said Senegal's workout could establish precedents for subsequent cases, adding negotiation risk to the immediate distribution of recoveries.

Hong Kong's access to dollar liquidity became the subject of a political request in Washington. House Select Committee on China chairman John Moolenaar asked Fed Chair Kevin Warsh to review the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's access to the FIMA repo facility, citing its role as a Chinese financial center and the crackdown on pro-democracy advocates. The Fed said it had received the letter and would respond.

FIMA permits approved foreign monetary authorities to obtain dollars against Treasuries, providing an alternative to selling holdings during funding stress. Its limit is $60 billion per counterparty per day, and changes require approval by the FOMC's Foreign Currency Subcommittee. Hong Kong held more than $258 billion of Treasuries in July. The request concerns access to that liquidity channel; it does not change the facility's terms.

U.S. municipal borrowing showed a more immediate cash-flow strain. Florida school districts have issued $1.4 billion of short-term tax-anticipation notes this year, 62% more than during all of 2025, according to LSEG. Declining enrollment, greater use of school-choice programs and the end of pandemic aid have pressured operating budgets. Local property-tax receipts arrive mainly between November and March, while payroll and other expenses continue throughout the year.

Fitch's Michael Rinaldi said rising reliance on these notes can indicate structural budget gaps or weaker cash balances. Hillsborough County used them for the first time in July and received a negative Fitch outlook in September as enrollment-related revenue losses and rising costs reduced reserves. Florida's school-choice funding reached approximately $4.41 billion in 2025-2026. The proposed November vote to largely eliminate local property taxes would exempt school levies, an important distinction for those revenues.

Apollo President Jim Zelter said Tuesday that governments and state-backed companies, particularly in Europe, were increasingly receptive to private capital as they confronted debt burdens. The firm is examining long-term financing and structures that move hard assets into subsidiaries to raise money, alongside opportunities in defense procurement. His comments describe an expanding potential funding role rather than a newly agreed sovereign transaction.

## Forward Market Significance

The Treasury's 10-year auction on October 7 and 30-year sale on October 8, both scheduled for 1 p.m. New York time, take the demand test beyond Tuesday's successful three-year offering. The long bond's small gain leaves particular significance in the reception to longer maturity supply. Japan's 30-year auction on Thursday will likewise test whether the buying seen at 10 years extends further along its curve.

The Fed's September meeting minutes arrive October 7 at 2 p.m. New York time. They will give more detail on the decision to begin raising rates, while Tuesday's firmer ADP reading and unchanged 3.7% GDPNow estimate provide a newer activity backdrop. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem is scheduled to speak October 8 and Boston Fed President Susan Collins on October 9. Initial claims on Thursday are expected at 200,000; continuing claims are expected at 1.710 million against 1.701 million previously.

Energy and inflation expectations offer separate tests of the bond rally's durability. Wednesday's EIA inventory report will provide the official stock reading after the API draw. September consumer inflation expectations are also due Wednesday, followed by the University of Michigan's preliminary October survey Friday. September U.S. CPI is scheduled for October 14. Societe Generale's diesel analysis makes the breadth and persistence of cost transmission consequential even if crude avoids another sharp rise.

Wednesday's MBA release will update mortgage conditions after a 7.3% 30-year rate and a 6% decline in applications in the preceding observation. That provides a more rate-sensitive demand test alongside the stronger employment and logistics readings.

India's policy decision comes Wednesday at 10 a.m. Mumbai time. Of 41 economists surveyed by Bloomberg, 35 expect a quarter-point repo-rate increase to 5.50%, with the others expecting no change. The prevailing expectation is that the RBI will retain a neutral stance. IDFC First Bank's Gaura Sen Gupta envisages a shallow cycle totaling 75 basis points by February to prevent the real policy rate turning negative as inflation rises; Oxford Economics' Alexandra Hermann Prasad instead argues that benign core inflation allows more time to support growth.

The accompanying forecasts and liquidity guidance will help determine the meaning of any increase. Citi's Samiran Chakraborty expects the inflation projection to rise by about 10 basis points from 5% and the growth forecast to be upgraded from 6.7% for the fiscal year through March 2027. With the rupee near a record low and excess bank cash still complicating transmission, a higher repo rate and the pace of liquidity absorption remain separate decisions. Karur Vysya Bank's VRC Reddy expects the 10-year yield to settle around its current 7.23% if the RBI raises rates while staying neutral; a more restrictive signal on rates and liquidity could, in his view, take the yield toward 7.38%-7.40% in coming months.

section_summaries.summary: Buying returned after the Treasury selloff without much relief in long-term borrowing costs. The recovery held despite oil’s rebound and stronger U.S. activity readings, with lower real yields outweighing a rise in inflation compensation. French fiscal pledges and strong demand for Air Liquide offered respite, while corporate financing remained available despite sharp differences in collateral protection and creditor recoveries.

Australia’s household sentiment deteriorated after tightening, while Czech inflation strengthened the case for another increase. overall_summary.headline: Treasuries retain modest gains after oil rebounds, with little relief at 30 years
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries recovered on October 6 after early oil weakness encouraged buying, then held their gains through a well-received $58 billion 3-year auction. The 10-year yield fell 2.53 basis points to 5.2815%, while the 30-year slipped just 0.4 basis point to 5.6599%. At 10 years, the real yield fell 3.22 basis points, more than accounting for the nominal decline as breakeven inflation rose 0.69 basis point.

Brent reversed its early decline to finish above $100 as increased exports through Hormuz competed with continuing tanker risks. Firmer weekly employment growth and logistics activity, alongside an import-led widening of the trade deficit, offered little evidence of broad economic weakening. Equities reached records and U.S. high-yield and hard-currency emerging-market spreads tightened noticeably.

France’s bond market found respite amid new fiscal pledges, while strong demand for Air Liquide’s debt showed investors distinguishing internationally diversified companies from their sovereign. Its fixed-rate tranches were set to price below the French government curve. Corporate financing continued to clear, but collateral rights and insolvency recoveries left creditors with sharply different outcomes. The U.S. 10- and 30-year auctions will test whether demand extends to longer maturities.
overall_summary.summary: Early oil weakness and firm demand at the 3-year auction supported a recovery driven by lower real yields, even as inflation compensation edged higher and fresh U.S. data showed resilient activity.
